open_points.subject: actor attribution for records written during compound operations
open_points.text: “Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27” and “The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record,” but TrialExecution, AdmissionVerdict, NodeExecution and EffectAttempt name no actor, and operations such as submit_implementation and start_run mix caller-triggered work with automatic kernel work.
open_points.question: Which actor must be recorded for each record produced by admission, an explicit try, run advancement, approval handling, resume and startup recovery, and where is that actor stored?
options: Use the request actor for all records produced during that request and kernel during recovery
Use kernel for automatic executions, verdicts and advancement, while retaining the request actor only on the initiating or decision record
Add separate initiating_actor and executing_actor facts where both matter
open_points.default_guess: Use the caller for authored or explicitly requested observations, use kernel for automatic admission, activation and recovery records, and add an actor fact to every record that otherwise cannot distinguish them.

open_points.subject: flow constant schema
open_points.text: compose_flow_version takes “constants with declared classes,” but later says “A constant's StoredValue takes the value_schema and class the composing agent declared with it (State 6, decision 5), never its target's.” No accepted State 6 decision is present and the operation input does not include the declared schema.
open_points.question: Must every constant request carry its own value_schema, and exactly which constant facts participate in validation and flow-version identity?
options: Require an explicit value_schema and disclosure_class on every constant
Derive the schema from the target port while requiring only the class
Infer the schema from the literal value
open_points.default_guess: Require each constant to carry an explicit canonical value_schema and disclosure_class, both included in its StoredValue and flow-version identity.

open_points.subject: functions.try_implementation
open_points.text: Its Observable effect is “None,” while its State impact is “One record_trial_execution per case” and TrialExecution records are durable.
open_points.question: Is trying an implementation a durable state-changing operation, or must its evidence be returned without persistence?
options: Persist one TrialExecution per executed case
Return transient evidence and write no records
open_points.default_guess: Persist one TrialExecution per case, as required by A04 and the named store change.

open_points.subject: trial execution answers
open_points.text: try_implementation returns “outcome, output digests, pass or output_mismatch,” while “Records reach a caller as they are, with values resolved by module:surface: a value StoredValue as its JSON content.” TrialExecution value outputs are StoredValue references.
open_points.question: Do try, repair and inspection answers expose successful JSON output values, or only their digests and metadata?
options: Resolve and return JSON values, subject to personal-data masking
Return only output digests and file facts
Return values only to the owner and digests to every agent regardless of class
open_points.default_guess: Resolve JSON outputs for the owner and agents except where A07 requires personal-data masking; return only facts for file outputs.

open_points.subject: surface handling of internal_error
open_points.text: State 3 says “every failure it answers internal_error ... is answered first, and then surface.serve_kernel ends the process,” while State 5 says only that surface answers internal_error and separately says “stop_required ... ends the process.” surface.serve_kernel also mentions process termination only for stop_required.
open_points.question: Must every request-level internal_error terminate the kernel after the response, or only stop_required?
options: Terminate after every internal_error response
Terminate only for stop_required
Terminate only for store and cleanup errors, but continue after other internal errors
open_points.default_guess: Terminate after every request-level internal_error, following A14 rule 7 and State 3.

open_points.subject: store.page_records with mutable filters
open_points.text: The token is “the store position of the last item returned; the next page starts below it,” but a record whose filtered status changes between pages is said to “leave or enter the pages still to come.” A newer record that did not match the first page cannot enter a later page below that cursor.
open_points.question: What guarantee applies when a lifecycle field used by the filter changes between pages?
options: Position-cursor semantics: changed records above the cursor may be omitted and clients restart to see them
Snapshot the filter membership at the first page
Use a query cursor capable of revisiting records whose mutable field newly matches
open_points.default_guess: Use strict position-cursor semantics and state that newly matching records above the cursor are not seen without restarting pagination.

open_points.subject: agent view of an EffectApproval preview
open_points.text: The preview contains “the built request and the input values,” including a full URL, headers and body, while “an agent receives a personal-data value or file only as digest and class.” Personal values may already be embedded in path segments, query parameters or a JSON body.
open_points.question: How is the built-request portion of an approval preview transformed for an agent when it embeds personal_data?
options: Return a structured preview and replace each personal field occurrence with digest and class
Omit the whole request description when any personal input contributes to it
Return only request_digest plus separately masked inputs to agents
open_points.default_guess: Return request_digest and a structured request description whose personal-derived components are replaced by digest and class, never the raw URL or body containing them.

open_points.subject: approval coverage of multipart requests
open_points.text: Owner decision 18 says approval covers the “fully built request” and “Any difference at send ... asks again,” but A10 excludes the multipart boundary from the content type and body description so “equal parts give equal descriptions.”
open_points.question: Does changing the multipart boundary between approval and sending invalidate the approval?
options: No; multipart boundaries are explicitly outside approval identity
Yes; freeze the exact boundary before approval and include it in request_digest
Allow a changed boundary only when the exact encoded body remains otherwise equivalent
open_points.default_guess: Treat the boundary as an explicitly permitted non-semantic difference and exclude it from approval identity, following the later detailed A10 rule.

open_points.subject: spool-ceiling failure after a service response
open_points.text: store.spool_file returns refused over a spool ceiling and says “the caller concludes the element ... contract_violation for an operation,” while effects.reach_operation_element says “any refusal or error of a module it calls that is not one of those is internal_error.” The cumulative run-spool ceiling is known only when effects calls store after the HTTP response.
open_points.question: How must effects.reach_operation_element handle store.spool_file refusing a service file because of a spool ceiling?
options: Record contract_violation; for a non-read attempt record applied, and for a read write the read outcome
Convert the store refusal to internal_error and leave a non-read attempt in_flight
Return a surface refusal without concluding the element
open_points.default_guess: Record contract_violation, with a non-read EffectAttempt concluded applied, as A09, A15 and State 3 require.

open_points.subject: store.open_store initialization
open_points.text: open_store says “Take the exclusive lock, check the data directory and remove temporary files before any record is read,” but does not say what happens when the configured data directory, database or internal areas do not yet exist.
open_points.question: Does first start create and initialize the data directory and store, or refuse until an operator creates them?
options: Create an absent directory and empty store with private permissions
Require the directory to exist but create the database and internal areas
Require the complete empty store layout to be provisioned externally
open_points.default_guess: Require the configured data directory to exist with private ownership and permissions, then initialize the database and internal subdirectories inside it.

open_points.subject: store.open_store compatibility and corruption
open_points.text: Its Errors list names only “the lock held, a directory not private, or a symbolic link”; no behavior is specified for an unreadable, corrupt or incompatible existing database and file layout.
open_points.question: How does open_store report a corrupt store or a store created by an incompatible schema version?
options: Refuse start with a bounded compatibility or corruption reason
Return internal_error and stop start
Migrate compatible older schemas automatically
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup with a bounded reason and perform no automatic migration unless a later release explicitly defines one.

open_points.subject: functions.roll_back_slot eligibility
open_points.text: The operation says “Activate an earlier implementation,” while its enforcement only requires an implementation of the current contract version with an admitted verdict over the current corpus.
open_points.question: What makes an implementation “earlier”: any admitted non-current implementation, one submitted before the current implementation, or one that previously held an activation?
options: Any non-current implementation of the current contract version with the required verdict
Only an implementation submitted before the currently active implementation
Only an implementation that was previously activated
open_points.default_guess: Allow any non-current implementation of the current contract version that has an admitted verdict over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input boundary
open_points.text: The operation takes “One JSON value” but must refuse “a duplicate key,” and surface is said to turn incoming “JSON text” into canonical form with it. Duplicate keys are no longer observable after ordinary JSON parsing into a value.
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes accept raw JSON bytes/text and perform duplicate-aware parsing, or does another surface parser reject duplicates before passing a parsed value?
options: Accept raw JSON text and parse it with duplicate-key detection
Accept a parsed value plus parser evidence that no duplicate occurred
Make surface own duplicate-aware parsing and let canonical_bytes accept only parsed values
open_points.default_guess: Let surface perform duplicate-aware parsing of raw request JSON and pass only validated parsed values to canonical_bytes.

open_points.subject: service api_base_url validation and joining
open_points.text: An instance address is accepted when it is “an absolute http or https URL with a host,” and the request URL is the api_base_url “without a trailing / followed by the declared path.” The text does not constrain user information, query, fragment, base paths, percent encoding or how many trailing slashes are removed.
open_points.question: Which api_base_url forms are valid, and what exact URL results when it contains a path, query, fragment, user information or trailing slashes?
options: Reject user information, query and fragment; allow an optional base path and join it byte-for-byte to the operation path
Require a pure origin URL with no path other than /
Allow every absolute HTTP URL and use a standard URL-resolution algorithm
open_points.default_guess: Reject user information, query and fragment; allow a base path, remove one terminal slash from that path, and append the declared absolute operation path without further normalization.

open_points.subject: manifest_location and manifest_revision
open_points.text: The installation supplies “where the platform manifest is read and the repository revision it is read at,” and bindings reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision`, but no operation defines how a file is obtained at that revision.
open_points.question: Is manifest_location a checked-out immutable directory, a version-control repository requiring object lookup at manifest_revision, or another revision-addressable source?
options: Read the file directly from a directory already materialized at the configured revision
Treat manifest_location as a Git repository and read the file object at manifest_revision
Require a host-provided revision-aware manifest adapter
open_points.default_guess: Treat manifest_location as a Git repository and read the named file from the exact configured revision without changing the working tree.
